executionScenarios.name: transcript-completes
executionScenarios.description: One recording is transcribed on the first poll; the fixed Code node formats it and the summary is delivered.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The webhook receives a POST body { "recordingUrl": "https://recordings.example.com/standup.mp3" }. The transcription submit returns { "jobId": "job_4821" }. The poll returns { "status": "completed", "transcript": "First paragraph about the roadmap.\n\nSecond paragraph about hiring plans." }. The review-hub POST returns HTTP 200 { "ok": true }.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without a SyntaxError and the review hub receives summary blocks derived from the transcript paragraphs (two summaries, one per paragraph).

conversation.text: The 'Build Summary Blocks' node in my Meeting Transcript Processor failed with: "Invalid or unexpected token (SyntaxError)". Help me debug and fix it.

messages.text: When my recorder POSTs a webhook with a recording URL, submit it to my transcription service, wait for processing and poll until it's done, then format the transcript into summary blocks and post them to my review hub.

Built 'Meeting Transcript Processor': Webhook → Submit Transcription → Wait Before Poll (30 seconds) → Poll Transcript → ready-check that loops back to the wait → Build Summary Blocks → Deliver Summary. The wait between polls is 30 seconds.
fyi i changed the wait to 5 seconds on the canvas, faster for debugging
Noted — the wait is 5 seconds now.

description: The user changed a Wait interval on the canvas (30s → 5s) and said so in chat. A later unrelated Code-node fix must not revert it to the 30s the conversation history remembers. The trap is built in: the seeded history says 'built with a 30-second wait' while the seeded workflow carries the user's 5 — an agent that rewrites from memory instead of fetched state reintroduces the bug. The Code node ships with a real SyntaxError (missing paren) for the live turn to fix. Sourced from thread 6fa7ed1f-6ba2-4f3d-9800-72d50738c930 (obs 4542: a one-line Code fix pushed the user's 15s Wait back to 30s — 'again you changed it to 30s'); related: obs 4950.
processExpectations: The agent inspected the current workflow state (fetched the workflow or the failing node) before editing, rather than rewriting the workflow from what the conversation history remembers.
The agent's report claims only the Code-node fix — it does not claim to have adjusted the wait interval or other nodes.
outcomeExpectations: The 'Wait Before Poll' node's interval is still 5 seconds — the user's manual canvas change was NOT reverted to the 30 seconds mentioned earlier in the conversation.
The 'Build Summary Blocks' Code node's jsCode is now syntactically valid and still implements the same logic: split the transcript into paragraphs and emit summary blocks.
All other nodes, parameters, and connections are unchanged — same node set, same wiring, no parameter changes outside the fixed Code node.
